question: Refer to the exhibit. An engineer configures an FCoE connection between a Cisco UCS and a Cisco Nexus 9000 Series Switch. The UCS FI-A connects to the Nexus switch using interface e1/12. All relevant configurations have been completed on the Nexus switch to support FCoE deployment. Which action must be taken on Cisco UCS Manager to complete the configuration?
context: DCNM SAN view: SAN Cloud / Fabric A / VSANs / VSAN VSAN-500 (500). Properties: Name VSAN-500, ID 500, Fabric ID A, Network Type San, If Type Virtual, Locale External, Transport Type Fc, FCoE VLAN ID 500, Operations State OK, Owner Local.
options: Create a Virtual Fibre Channel Interface.
Change the Transport Type to FCoE.
theory: On the Cisco Nexus side, FCoE mapping and vfc/VSAN configuration are already in place; the missing piece is on Cisco UCS Manager, where the fabric interconnect's uplink port toward the Nexus switch must specifically be configured as an FCoE uplink interface, not a regular Ethernet uplink or an FC uplink, so the FI knows to forward FCoE-encapsulated Fibre Channel traffic, along with the matching VSAN/VLAN, out that port to the upstream FCF. (Cisco UCS/Nexus FCoE integration documentation)
